einzeiler: Nick Frost on his mental health collapse, fatherhood and playing Hagrid in the new series.
kurzfassung: Actor Nick Frost opens up about his mental health collapse six years ago and how it transformed his perspective on life and acting. He discusses the intense anxiety he still experiences on set, his unexpected casting as Hagrid, and his journey overcoming food addiction. The conversation also touches on his working-class roots, early fame, and finding peace with a small circle of loved ones.
stichpunkte: Experiencing a psychological collapse six years ago fundamentally changed his mental health and approach to acting.
He treats his time on set as a place of structure and calm compared to the unpredictability of real life.
He struggles with severe pre-shoot anxiety and line-learning nerves, often falling violently sick before day one.
Securing the role of Hagrid in the upcoming series brought a massive boost to his self-esteem.
He has lost 200 pounds and openly addresses his long-standing addiction to food rooted in childhood trauma.
Reflecting on his working-class background, he admits to past feelings of shame and unworthiness regarding acting.
He shares a deep appreciation for his wife and values their quiet life raising their young children together.

clips.hook: A life-changing event shifted his entire approach to work and mental health.
clips.text: An unspecified incident several years prior altered his perspective, making him realize that his previous high-energy persona was unsustainable for his mental well-being.

clips.hook: He lost 200 pounds and confronted his lifelong addiction to food.
clips.text: Having shed a massive amount of weight, he recognized that secret binge eating served as a coping mechanism stemming from a difficult childhood.

beschreibung:
Nick Frost (Shaun of the Dead, How to Train Your Dragon) joins us this week for one of the most open and disarming conversations we have had. Nick opens up about the psychological collapse 6 years ago that completely rebuilt him and the version of himself he had to let go of. We also get into manifesting the role of Hagrid in the new Harry Potter series by writing the name 12,000 times, the hypervigilance that came from a violent childhood, losing 200 pounds, and why he is a better person on set than he is at home.
